newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel stockholders okay Amatil deal.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel stockholders okay Amatil deal.

text.p: Shareholders of San Miguel Corp on Tuesday approved a share swap between subsidiary Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI) and Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil.
However, the government which has a majority shareholding, urged the company to seek better terms for the deal.
Early this month, San Miguel said it planned to merge its 70 percent owned subsidiary Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI) in exchange for a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil.
The approval of the controversial deal, which has been criticised by some analysts for being more advantageous to Amatil, was given at the annual general meeting attended by some 2,000 shareholders.
Magtanggol Gunigundo, chairman of the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG), said though the government backed the merger it urged San Miguel to seek better terms.

The PCGG is a government agency formed to pursue assets of deposed President Ferdinand Marcos in the belief they were illegally acquired during his 20-year rule. The San Miguel shares held by the PCGG are part of assets sequestered by the government.
"We want a fair valuation that will increase representation in the board of Amatil from three board seats," Gunigundo said.
"San Miguel should also be represented not only on the board but also by a Treasurer," he added.
San Miguel Chairman Andres Soriano had earlier defended planned merger but responding to Gunigundo's comments, said: "Obviously we will see what we can do."
